ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZi-xBA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDJt_8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 79, "title": "Correct S-DSP end-without-loop header muting and continued silent BRR processing", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `64da1ba6249a451d6d7191409d74b6b0e792dd6d`, `Dsp::decode` plays an entire end-without-loop block before clearing its envelope and deactivating the voice at the following boundary. Deactivation then prevents further BRR processing and ENDX events. See [`dsp.rs`, decode and sample](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/64da1ba6249a451d6d7191409d74b6b0e792dd6d/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs#L63-L113).

The [Issue #77 validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/64da1ba6249a451d6d7191409d74b6b0e792dd6d/docs/issue-77-validation.md#sample-api-conventions-and-remaining-uncertainty) explicitly identifies this discrepancy: the cited references describe header-stage muting/release and continued internal fetching. Its terminal control deliberately preserves the existing approximation. This is the incomplete behavior prioritized by the latest assessment; it is separate from the completed live-directory correction. The supplied context lists no open Issues.

This affects finite sample termination and observable DSP status. Passing tests that preserve the approximation does not establish hardware correctness.

## Expected outcome

Implement the bounded sample-level terminal-header lifecycle for stable BRR data and nonzero pitch:

- Header low bits `00` and `10` continue sequentially; the loop bit alone does not terminate a block.
- Header low bits `01` force the envelope to zero and enter release when the header is processed. Do not play the terminal payload at the previous envelope or substitute an ordinary gradual KOFF fade.
- Header low bits `11` retain audible looping behavior.
- A silent terminal voice continues pitch/BRR processing. End-bit boundaries still select the current directory loop pointer and report ENDX, including when the loop bit is clear. Silence must not be implemented by permanently stopping the voice's internal work.
- ENDX remains sticky until a write clears it; later completed end blocks can reassert it. Header muting and block-completion ENDX are distinct events. KON clears the selected voice's ENDX and restarts through its start pointer.
- Later directory, SRCN, ADSR or GAIN changes cannot revive the released voice without KON. Preserve BRR progression/history while silent rather than repeatedly resetting decoder state.

**Specification basis and reconciliation:** use [Anomie/jwdonal S-DSP revision 1212](https://gist.github.com/nyanpasu64/a0d916ce6924912a7116682bf778e9a0#file-apudsp_jwdonal-txt), BRR DECODING, ENDX and SOUND GENERATION; [Fullsnes BRR Samples](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm#snesapudspbrrsamples), Loop/End bits; and Shay Green/blargg's pinned primary research implementation, [`SPC_DSP.cpp`](https://github.com/snes9xgit/snes9x/blob/8028d3b6ca994f21fdff220d513a08382e37afc3/apu/bapu/dsp/SPC_DSP.cpp), especially V3c and V4. Reconcile header-triggered envelope zero/release, end-bit-only pointer redirection, continued fetching and ENDX publication explicitly. Distinguish simplified descriptions such as “end+mute” from stopping internal processing.

These external links are recorded by the repository; this read-only planning pass did not fetch them. Before freezing expectations, substantiate the detailed contract from the attributed sections and correct any unsupported interpretation with documented evidence. Existing tests are not specification authority.

**Scope:** terminal-header handling, the processing-versus-silence distinction needed to support it, focused tests, provenance and validation documentation. Retain Issue #77's live-directory behavior. If shared release-zero logic must change, justify that dependency and protect ordinary KOFF behavior.

**Non-goals and uncertainty:** no DSP subcycle pipeline rewrite, exact physical header-prefetch/KON alignment, zero-pitch header-fetch timing, torn writes, SPC/DSP or echo/RAM races, unrelated NON/PMON specification corrections, reset-retention changes, frontend work, firmware or commercial ROM acquisition. Document how header processing maps into the existing eager scalar decoder; do not present its API call numbers as physical DSP timing. Full physical header timing remains outstanding.

## Context and reproduction

Inspect these existing tests before changing expectations:

- [`dsp_directory.rs::normal_blocks_ignore_loop_bit_and_end_without_loop_stays_silent`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/64da1ba6249a451d6d7191409d74b6b0e792dd6d/crates/snes-core/tests/dsp_directory.rs#L268-L299) expects both the normal and terminal blocks to play with ENVX=64, followed by permanent silence without renewed ENDX.
- [`regression.rs::dsp_endx_reports_brr_ends_independently_of_looping`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/64da1ba6249a451d6d7191409d74b6b0e792dd6d/crates/snes-core/tests/regression.rs#L1151-L1200) covers all eight voices and four flag combinations, but permits reassertion after clearing only for end+loop.
- [`dsp_envelope_tests.rs::release_retrigger_soft_reset_and_reconstruction_isolate_hidden_state`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/64da1ba6249a451d6d7191409d74b6b0e792dd6d/crates/snes-core/src/dsp_envelope_tests.rs#L118-L152) asserts an internal inactive state at release zero. Review this assumption if the shared lifecycle changes; retain independently justified envelope and retrigger assertions.

Construct an original filter-0 sequence with a nonzero normal block followed by a distinct nonzero `01` block. Use direct GAIN 64, pitch `$1000`, disabled echo writes and nonzero stereo volumes. The existing code keeps ENVX=64 while consuming the terminal payload, then stops. Also start directly on a terminal block whose loop pointer selects another end block, clear ENDX after its first event, and advance through another boundary. The current code cannot produce another event after deactivation. These observations follow from source inspection; no suites were rerun during planning.

Use the existing firmware-free uploaded-guest pattern and [original-test provenance convention](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/64da1ba6249a451d6d7191409d74b6b0e792dd6d/tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md#original-live-directory-spc700-guest-and-brr-data-approved). Generate original guest instructions, directory entries, BRR payloads and numerical expectations from source. Do not import another emulator's implementation or output as the oracle.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the source reconciliation above, including supported semantics, any conflicts and the chosen sample-API mapping. Implement terminal-header zero/release and continued silent processing. Do not defer muting until terminal-block completion or deactivate the decoder solely because this envelope is zero.
- [ ] Add focused original public-API tests, for example `crates/snes-core/tests/dsp_brr_end.rs`. Cover terminal-at-start and normal-to-terminal transitions with nonzero signed filter-0 data; flags `00/10/11` controls; direct GAIN and ADSR; pitches `$1000`, `$1800` and `$3000`; and a second unaffected voice. Assert numerical stereo PCM, ENVX, OUTX and ENDX around the separately identified header and end events. Derive expectations independently of production decoding/state logic.
- [ ] Demonstrate continued processing after silence: clear ENDX, observe its later reassertion through a known end-block chain, and test a stable live loop-pointer change while silent. Verify that gain/directory edits do not restore output and that a subsequent KON selects the current start pointer and restores the established key-on behavior. Add narrowly scoped private-state tests if necessary to distinguish genuine decoding/history progression from fabricated status events; no new public inspection API is required.
- [ ] Replace the source-contradicted terminal expectations identified above, retaining sequential-block, end+loop, eight-voice ENDX, live-directory, envelope, noise, pitch, mixing and echo coverage. Document each changed legacy expectation and its source justification. Run the new discriminators against the baseline in an isolated checkout and record behavioral failures; compilation failures do not count as evidence.
- [ ] Add an original SPC700 guest uploaded through the existing firmware-free protocol. Configure/read DSP registers through `$F2/$F3`, record terminal ENVX/OUTX/ENDX and clear/reassert results into RAM, and use bounded acknowledgements. Assert independent PCM/register anchors. Compare whole versus irregular `Apu::tick` partitions for every PCM sample, all DSP registers, RAM and output ports at fixed checkpoints. Partition equality establishes determinism, not physical timing. Document original MIT provenance.
- [ ] Pass the focused tests and workspace checks:

  ```sh
  cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test dsp_brr_end
  cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test dsp_directory
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
  cargo test --workspace --locked
  ```

- [ ] Pass the existing source-built hardware and browser gates documented in README, using their unchanged audited pins and provenance:

  ```sh
  python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
  cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
  python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
  python3 tools/hardware-tests.py \
    --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" \
    --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" \
    --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
  python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
  python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
  python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
  npm --prefix web ci
  npm --prefix web run build
  cd web
  npx playwright install chromium
  npm test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
  ```

  Apply README's compiler-selection or test-port options where needed. Preserve cleared Castle/Memory source pins, licensing, expected ROM hashes, replay durations/routes, freeze controls and numerical/live audio assertions. Report actual results and any failures or unperformed checks; do not weaken game regressions to accommodate the fix.

- [ ] Update README and the validation/provenance records with baseline discriminators, final results and remaining limits. Keep all 24 inventory scopes: partial `cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-hires`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-voices`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo`, `dsp-timing`; unimplemented `ppu-raster`, `pal`. None becomes verified. Remaining voice work includes independent BRR-filter 1–3 evidence, exhaustive interpolation phases, simultaneous key/mixing combinations, KON-delay selection changes and physical header/directory/key timing. Do not claim full hardware accuracy, commercial compatibility or completion of Issue #3.

## Optional validation

None required beyond the pre-merge checks.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
